column5: Lich also rebuilds the command as `drag <name> <target>` from the earlier grab line. Only the simple repair is expressed here: dragging a body is not travel, and a router that plans one is answering a question nobody asked.
You fell. Stand before trying again.
Your disk did not follow. Send it again; nothing to fix.
Twice, as Lich does. One retreat moves you one range band.
Climbing and swimming want both hands.
Some rooms will not admit someone nobody can see.
The game refuses to let you walk off and leave it.
Sitting, lying, kneeling. Thirteen ways to be told to get up.
The map says `go`, the game wants `climb`. A correction the overlay should eventually carry so nobody pays the round trip.
The same mistake in the other direction.
The largest branch, and the one that matters most: twenty-six ways for the game to say the exit is not there. Lich returns false, which its map layer takes as licence to delete the edge.

A ticket, a guest pass, a club membership, a reputation. The exit is real and this character may not use it -- Lich returns nil *specifically* so the direction is not removed from the map. This is the Silverwood Manor case.

DIVERGENCE FROM LICH. Lich returns *true* here, which claims you arrived; you did not, and every command after it is sent from the wrong room. You need a light source. Recorded as unavailable, which is what it is.
Lich polls for the line for three seconds. The text is the signal, so a client waits for it rather than for a duration.
A boltstone apparatus discharging into you.

The ice. Six seconds of roundtime and you are on your back, in the room you started in. This is the recovery; the four-second pause in `conditions` is the avoidance, and a walk needs both -- the pause is skippable at high Survival, and the recovery never is.
Lich also waits out stun *before* every send, so seeing this at all means the stun landed between the check and the command.
Sailor's Grief. The swim messages are progress, not failure.
The silvery thread needs both hands. Lich refills them on arrival, which is why `empty-hands` implies a refill.

Sigil of Resolve. Lich returns nil when the character does not know it, so a client without the spell should treat this as `unavailable` -- the remedy is conditional on knowing 9704, which is a character fact and belongs in the snapshot, not here.
Vertigo, a guard checking you in, a shimmering field. Nothing is wrong; it simply did not take this time.
Server backpressure: more commands in flight than the subscription allows. The only failure here caused by the client rather than the world, and the one a batching walker will meet first.
`...Wait 3 seconds.` -- the server's own roundtime refusal. The count is in the message, so a client reads it there rather than sleeping a constant.
Open it once. If it is still closed it is locked, and opening it again will not help.
Several doors, and the map named the ordinal wrong. Lich walks the ordinal up one each time; the detail here is the first step of that, and a client that implements the walk can keep going.
